# Snice

> Decorator-driven web component framework with differential rendering, routing, controllers, and 130+ UI components. Zero dependencies. MIT licensed.

- Version: 6.1.x
- Website: https://snice.dev
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/snice
- CDN: https://cdn.snice.dev

## Where to Find Information

### For AI Assistants
- [llms-full.txt](https://snice.dev/llms-full.txt) — Complete API reference, architecture rules, all decorators, template syntax, router, pitfalls

### For Humans
- https://snice.dev/guide.html — Getting started guide
- https://snice.dev/components.html — Live interactive component demos
- https://snice.dev/decorators.html — Decorator reference with examples

## What Snice Is

A TypeScript web component framework using TC39 decorators and configurable shadow/light render roots. Components may extend `HTMLElement` directly or the optional `SniceElement` convention base. There is no virtual DOM; differential rendering patches only changed DOM parts.

Four building blocks:
- **Elements** (`@element`) — Visual components. Receive data via properties, emit events.
- **Pages** (`@page`) — Routable views. Handle API calls and orchestration.
- **Controllers** (`@controller`) — Reusable non-visual behaviors. Attach by class in templates (`controller=${MyController}`, preferred) or by name in raw HTML (`controller="name"`).
- **Layouts** (`@layout`) — Persistent page wrappers (nav, sidebar).

## Quick Start

```bash
npx snice create-app my-app
```

```typescript
import { element, property, render, styles, html, css } from 'snice';

@element('my-counter')
class MyCounter extends HTMLElement {
  @property({ type: Number }) count = 0;

  @styles()
  css() { return css`:host { display: block; }`; }

  @render()
  template() {
    return html`<button @click=${() => this.count++}>${this.count}</button>`;
  }
}
```

## Usage Modes

### npm (bundled apps)
```typescript
import 'snice/components/button/snice-button';
```

### CDN (no build step)
```html
<script src="https://cdn.snice.dev/runtime/snice-runtime.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.snice.dev/components/snice-button.min.js"></script>
```

### React
```jsx
import { SniceButton } from 'snice/adapters/react';
```

## Key Warnings

- Snice is NOT Lit — don't import from `lit` or extend `LitElement`
- Use `@property()` for public attribute/property input and `@state()` for internal reactive state
- Direct JavaScript property writes preserve type and identity; conversion happens at the string attribute boundary
- `@state({ deep: true })` uses native Proxy/Reflect for nested objects, arrays, Map, and Set (modern browsers; no IE)
- Prefer direct bindings for known keys. Named spreads are for dynamic or forwarded bags.
- Full declarative rendering syntax: https://snice.dev/docs.html#rendering
- Exact binding-channel and sentinel semantics: https://snice.dev/docs.html#bindings
- `page` decorator comes from `Router()`, not from `'snice'` exports
- Elements are visual only — no fetch/API calls (use pages/controllers)
